paper.title: Advancing extrapolative predictions of material properties through learning to learn using extrapolative episodic training
paper.research_summary: This study develops a meta-learning methodology—extrapolative episodic training (E2T)—to enhance the ability of machine learning models to predict material properties beyond the distribution of training data. Using attention-based matching neural networks (MNNs) trained on arbitrarily generated extrapolative episodes, the approach demonstrates superior generalization for unseen material domains in two case studies: predicting specific heat and refractive index of polymeric materials, and bandgap of hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites. The method enables rapid adaptation to target domains via fine-tuning with limited data.

tasks.objective: To develop a machine-learning methodology that enables extrapolative generalization—predicting physical properties of materials outside the domain covered by training data.
constraints: need to discover innovative materials from unexplored material spaces
input_requirements: material representation (e.g., Morgan fingerprint for polymers, crystal structure for perovskites)
output_goal: real-valued physical property prediction (y ∈ ℝ) for unseen material domains

evidence.text: The goal of materials science is to predict material properties beyond the data distribution range. This study presented a machine-learning methodology to address this fundamental challenge.
Central to this progress is the development of rapidly computable property predictors, which allow identifying novel materials with the desired properties from vast material spaces.
In this study, we leveraged the attention-based architecture of neural networks and a meta-learning algorithm to enhance extrapolative generalization capabilities.

evidence.text: Numerous episodes were generated from a given dataset D, each comprising a training set S and test set Q containing instances outside the training domain S.

For instance, (xi, yi) represents the physical property yi of a cellulose derivative xi, whereas Si represents a dataset from other polymer classes, such as conventional plastic resins. Alternatively, (xi, yi) can correspond to a compound containing element species that do not exist in the training compounds comprising Si.

stages.stage_name_raw: meta-training of MNNs via extrapolative episodic training (E2T)
stages.stage_goal: To train matching neural networks (MNNs) to learn the mapping y = f(x, S) using extrapolative episodes.

evidence.text: We employed a meta-learning algorithm30–34, commonly known as “learning to learn,” to impart extrapolative prediction capabilities to the MNNs.
E2T learning is formulated as ℓ2 loss minimization as follows: Jϕ = Σ(xi,yi,Si)∈T (yi − f(xi, Si))²

stages.stage_goal: To adapt pretrained meta-learners to target domains using limited data from those domains.
stage_input: small dataset from target domain (e.g., one polymer class, HOIP-GeF)
stage_output: fine-tuned predictor optimized for target domain

evidence.text: Fine-tuning was performed on the RadonPy dataset. In this experiment, a pretrained E2T model with a source data size of 38,000 was fine-tuned on data from the target domain corresponding to a particular polymer class.
An MNN pretrained by E2T with a source data size of 1248 (HOIP-GeF) or 1228 (HOIP-PbI) was fine-tuned on data, including data from the target domain.

In the polymer-property prediction experiments, 69,480 samples of Cp and 68,700 samples of the refractive index were used for the amorphous homopolymers. The data were generated using RadonPy36, which is a Python tool to construct a workflow for fully automated calculations of various polymeric properties using all-atom MD simulations.
This dataset included 1078 samples provided by Hayashi et al. (2022)36 and those newly generated by the RadonPy consortium.

Approximately 70,000 hypothetical polymers were generated using an N-gram-based polymer structure generator53 and classiﬁed into 20 polymer classes based on the classiﬁcation rules established by PolyInfo54.
The HOIP dataset40,41 contains 1345 perovskite compounds and their properties, including bandgaps, dielectric constants, and relative energies, calculated using the density functional theory.

To verify the generalizability of E2T, we conducted another experiment using a hybrid organic–inorganic perovskite (HOIP) dataset40,41, which includes 1345 perovskite structures and their properties, including bandgaps, as calculated through the density functional theory.
